newsitem.title: USA: NRC promises objective standards for watch list.
newsitem.headline: NRC promises objective standards for watch list.

text.p: The head of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said Wednesday that the agency would apply measurable objectives in a consistent fashion to determine which U.S. plants ought to be on the NRC's watch list of problem plants.
"What you're seeing is a more consistent application of criteria," Jackson told reporters following an NRC meeting. "It's a question of applying criteria in a fair way."
"There is no backing off," Jackson added.

During the meeting, the NRC removed New York Power Authority's Indian Point 3 plant from the agency's watch list, leaving 13 others on the list. NRC regional officials said the Indian Point plant had showed an improvement in the number and signficance of employee errors, and had corrected a variety of other problems.

Sam Collins, a senior NRC staff member, said the agency was trying to improve how plants were assessed for possible inclusion on the watch list. The agency's senior management committee now seeks input from several NRC departments on what plants ought to be discussed for inclusion, and is trying to make the process more transparent, he said.
Minutes of the NRC senior management meetings will now be made available to the public, he said.

The agency has been criticized by consumer groups in the past for moving too slowly to add plants to the list of those under close scrutiny by the NRC. But the industry claims that the list unfairly gives some plants a black eye, even when they are operating safely.
Last week, Sens. Joseph Biden and Joseph Lieberman released a General Accounting Office report which called for tougher safety measures by the agency.
"The process is improving but we have a ways to go," Collins said.
